title: The Mecca Pact: A New Treaty Organization, Just Like the Old One
gist: Argues the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye is not a CSTO analogue or a sign of NATO's demise, but a rerun of the Cold War's failed CENTO — a forum that will change nothing about how members actually plan their defense.

insights.claim: The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement is a collective security agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in early August, and has been variously read as a CSTO analogue and as evidence of a new regional order replacing NATO.
insights.speaker: Michael Coffey
insights.so_what: The pact is real but the interpretations attached to it are where the mispricing sits; do not re-rate regional defense exposure off the headline.
insights.locator: Much has been made of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement

insights.claim: Reports that the Mecca pact signals the end of NATO are overstated, and predictions that it will remake the region's security are off the mark when viewed with a longer historical lens.
insights.speaker: Michael Coffey
insights.so_what: Fade the 'post-NATO regional order' narrative trade; the alliance architecture in the region is more inertial than the commentary implies.
insights.quote: perhaps reports of NATO’s death are greatly exaggerated
insights.locator: Though, perhaps reports of NATO’s death

insights.claim: The closest historical analogue to the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement is the failed and largely forgotten Central Treaty Organization of the Cold War, not the CSTO or NATO.
insights.speaker: Michael Coffey
insights.so_what: Use CENTO's trajectory — paper commitments, no operational integration, quiet irrelevance — as the base case for pricing the pact's strategic impact.
insights.quote: MJDA resembles the failed and somewhat forgotten Central Treaty Organization (CENTO) of the Cold War

insights.claim: Member states of the Mecca pact and their neighbors are expected to continue their defense and security planning much as they did before, meaning the agreement should not change procurement, basing or force-posture assumptions.
insights.speaker: Michael Coffey
insights.so_what: Do not expect the pact to generate new joint procurement or integrated commands; defense-industrial forecasts built on it are likely to disappoint.
insights.locator: we can expect that, like CENTO, the member states themselves

insights.claim: A better modern template for the Mecca pact than any Western alliance is the Commonwealth of Independent States structure — an institution that functions as a venue for professed solidarity masking unresolved member grievances.
insights.speaker: Michael Coffey
insights.so_what: Read future Mecca pact summits as signalling exercises; the gap between communique language and member behavior is the thing to track.
insights.quote: a forum for warm promises and suppressed disgruntlement

insights.claim: The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement is unlikely to solve the problems it purports to confront and will accomplish little more than CENTO did.
insights.speaker: Michael Coffey
insights.so_what: A direct, falsifiable call: watch for the absence of joint exercises, standing headquarters or binding consultation mechanisms as confirmation.
insights.locator: MJDA is unlikely to solve the problems
